chapter: Germany, Buck's death and ideas about life
title: Stranded in Frankfurt: a band leader's offer and an agent's $15 a show
summary: At a cafe he knows the band leader but cannot take 20 marks a show; at the agent's office he is told Special Service pays $15 a show.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So I go to the Bonnhoff -- that's the railroad station, you know -- Bonnhoff. I go to the Bonnhoff which is right across the street from the American Airlines office and that's when I spy that this band that's playing in this club next to that that was American and I knew the band leader.
I went in and saw the band
leader with his band in there and told him about the situation. He said, I'll get the manager -- you do a number and I'll get the manager to give you a job here.

I did a number for him and man, I can't begin to tell you that I couldn't take the job. They wanted to give me 20 pounds, I think it was -- 20 pounds -- 20 marks, that's $5.00 -- isn't that right? Four marks is a dollar -- anyway, I think it was 20 marks a performance or 20 marks a show -- something like that. Anyhow, I couldn't take it and I didn't have no money in my pocket at all.

Now, don't forget, I'd already been to an agent's office who was Eddie Elkort--- I forget this guy's name, the agent. Anyhow I went to his office and the girl told me how much they pay for me, I told them I was from America, showed them my pictures and everything how long I did work, how much time I do on the stage and all and she says, the best thing we pay is $15 a show, I think. I says, 'Yeah?'

This is for special service now, this is. That's all the agents were booking over there, special service. That's what this was and that's what this guy, Lee Bouveau was booking, Special Service. However, I said no. So I showed them my pictures. Somebody got on the phone and I'm ready to go now, so when she got on the phone I'm ready to go. So she hollered to and says, "Don't you want to leave one of your pictures?" And to me I just said, just another picture left, that's all. I'll just give her another picture, it won't hurt me. Just give her the picture. I left it there, walked out. Understand.

Now I go down by the Bonnhoff as I told ya and I find that this guy that was going to give me a job for $20 a show, something like that and I couldn't take it. I couldn't take it. I told him what I wanted, they couldn't pay it. I didn't work. But I did a number for 'em. Okay?
So now I ain't got no job,
